dva-med-074.text: Before applying changes to CDK in production, the developer wants to see locally the CloudFormation generated and compared with what is implemented, listing the differences. CDK do, respectively, these two tasks?

cdk destroy and cdk start
cdk synth to synthesize the template and cdk diff to compare with the implanted stack
cdk bootstrap twice in a row

Destroy REMOVE stacks and init creates new projects — dangerously far from a change review.
Bootstrap prepares the account/Region for staff of the CDK — does not generate or compare templates.

dva-med-075.text: An environment of Elastic Beanstalk needs customizations in creation: install system packages, create configuration files and set environment options — all versioned along with application code. What Beanstalk mechanism supports this?
options: A make.config file in S3 read by Beanstalk
Edit to AMI Beanstalk base directly in production
Files .ebextensions (YAML/JSON) in the root of the application package, with sections such as packages, files, commands and option_settings
Access each instance via SSH and configure manually
dva-med-075.explanation: The .ebextensions customise the environment provisioning in a declarative and versioned way with the code — Beanstalk's official advanced configuration mechanism.
dva-med-075.hint: The 'EB extensions' folder inside the package: declaratory recipes that travel with each version.
optionRationales: The .ebextensions customise the environment provisioning in a declarative and versioned way with the code — Beanstalk's official advanced configuration mechanism.
Manual changes are lost when Beanstalk replaces instances — customisation must travel with the package.
Changing live AMIs is fragile; even custom AMIs must be built by process — and declarative configs go to .ebextensions.
There is no such mechanism — the official convention is the directory .eb extensions in the bundle.

dva-med-076.text: No. Elastic Beanstalk, the team wants the deployment policy MAIS safe for production: the new instances rise in a Auto Scaling Temporary group, are validated and only then replace the old ones — never mixing versions in the same instance and with simple rollback.?
options: Immutable: each deployer creates new instances with the new version and discards old ones only after validation
Turn off the environment and reconnect with the new version
Rolling without additional batch
All at eleven, being the fastest
dva-med-076.explanation: The immutable ensures that instances never receive in-place update: the healthy new proven fleet assumes and the old one is closed — failures discard only new instances, without touching production.
dva-med-076.hint: The policy in which nothing exists is 'reformed': only a new fleet is born — and the old one leaves after the test.
optionRationales: The immutable ensures that instances never receive in-place update: the healthy new proven fleet assumes and the old one is closed — failures discard only new instances, without touching production.
Maximum speed with total unavailability and rollback making new deployment — the opposite profile to the order.
Rolling updates instances EXISTENTES in lots, mixing versions and reducing capacity — less secure than the immutable.
Deliberate total downtime is not deployment policy — it's interruption.

dva-med-077.text: A service from the Amazon ECS needs blue/green implementations with validation before the exchange: the new set of tasks goes up behind a target test group, goes through verification and then the listener of the switch production for it. What integration enables this flow in the ECS?

Update the definition task and wait for the default rolling update
ECS with CodeDeploy (deployment controller CODE_DEPLOY), using two target groups and managed traffic displacement
Manually create a second cluster and exchange the DNS

The rolling update of the ECS replaces tasks gradually no MESMO target group — no parallel environment or validation before switching.
Manual orchestration of clusters and DNS is slow and prone to error — native integration automates everything.
Images version no ECR — and artifact versioning does not implement traffic switching.

dva-med-078.text: During the standard rolling update of a service ECS with 10 tasks, the team wants to ensure that there is never less than 8 tasks answering and never again 15 in simultaneous execution (cost). What parameters of the deployment configuration control these limits?

cpu and memory of the definition task
healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds isolated
dva-med-078.explanation: The two percentages govern the rolling of the ECS: the healthy minimum prevents degradation below the floor (8 of 10) and the maximum limits the temporary fleet inflated during replacement (15 of 10).
dva-med-078.hint: Two percentages on the desire: the 'health floor' and the 'swelling roof' during the exchange.

Resources per task size containers — not the amount of tasks in the bearing.

dva-med-079.text: Builds of CodeBuild are slow because each execution again lowers all dependencies (node_modules) and rebuilds Docker layers from scratch. CodeBuild reduces this time?

Cache of CodeBuild: caching of dependencies S3 (buildspec path) or local cache (including Docker layers) between builds
Roll the builds with less memory to force efficiency
Remove Build Tests
dva-med-079.explanation: The cache declared in the buildspec/project takes advantage of dependencies and layers between executions — cutting download minutes and rebuild each build.
dva-med-079.hint: Do not lower the world to each build: keep the dependencies and layers 'in the closet' between executions.
optionRationales: The cache declared in the buildspec/project takes advantage of dependencies and layers between executions — cutting download minutes and rebuild each build.
More time-limit tolerates slowness — does not eliminate it.
Less resources makes the build MAIS slow — efficiency is not born of scarcity.
Sacrificing Verification to Earn Minutes Quality Exchange for Speed — Cache Wins Time Without Quality Cost.

dva-med-080.text: A team wants to activate a new feature gradually in production SEM new deployment: link the feature to 10% of users, monitor and expand — with configuration validation and automatic reversal if alarms go off. AWS is specialized in this configuration management and feature flags?

dva-med-081.text: A stack of CloudFormation contains a bank RDS The team wants to prevent accidental stack updates from replacing or excluding this specific resource, requiring explicit release for changes in it. CloudFormation apply that protection?

Stack policy denying Update:Replace and Update:Delete to the bank's logical resource

Rename Resource to PROTEGITED_Do Not Delete
dva-med-081.explanation: The stack policy is the document that governs what updates can play: protecting the critical resource, any destructive operation in it fails until the policy is temporarily released — guard-rail against accidents.
